chapters.title: Border
paragraphs: Tamsin crossed the border into Velar on the last day of autumn. She carried one letter and one rule from the guild.
The Velarians drank their coffee black and their wine warm. Tamsin learned both habits in a week. She kept the coffee habit.
In the market the Guildsmen kept to their own side of the square. They wore grey coats and spoke quietly.
A Velarian porter carried her bag to the inn. Tamsin tipped the man and the man bowed twice.
The guild had agents in every town. Tamsin met three of them before the week was out. She liked none of them.
An Ostrene merchant offered her a seat at his table. The Ostrene always sat near the fire and never near the door.
Tamsin ate with the Ostrene and the Velarians together. She noticed that nobody mentioned the guild.
The Guildsmen came to her room on the fourth night. They asked about the letter and did not sit down.
Tamsin said the letter was for the guild alone. She did not raise her voice. The Guildsmen exchanged a glance and withdrew.
In the morning a Velarian child brought her bread and a note. The note was unsigned.
She read it twice by the window. It named a place in the old town, an hour, and nothing more.
Tamsin went to the old town at the hour named. The Ostrene merchant was waiting beside the fountain.
He said the guild could not be trusted, and that the Velarians knew it. Tamsin asked why the merchant was telling her.
Because you are honest, said the merchant, and the guild has no use for honest people.
Tamsin walked back through the market alone. The Guildsmen watched her pass and did not follow.
She burned the unsigned note in the inn's stove. The guild would never learn what it had said.
At the end of the month Tamsin returned the letter unopened. The guild accepted it without comment.
In the district everyone knew Tamsin, and nobody had a bad word for Tamsin.
Years afterwards people still asked about Tamsin, though few could say why.
